title: Dogfood Hardening
objective: Harden Meeting Ingest against what real HTV runs on released builds expose: extraction quality (semantic_guidance 1.1 and the spot-check backlog), run-flow friction (the date gate), artifact-contract gaps (Decisions status vocabulary, third-party sensitivity), attestation, and consumer update policy.
status_summary: Anonymization sweep complete and T2-verified: live docs, plans, discovery log, and the docx test fixture now use role terms (the reference consumer, the secondary consumer) and corpus IDs (legacy corpus A/B); AGENTS.md carries the standing Identifiers rule (invented example names, contents-frozen/filenames-normalized boundary, CLI-managed state clause); the client-named session filename was normalized with citations repaired in two board records as pure link fixes. Review fix set applied: pre-engine gloss narrowing corrected (binding OB-002-1 clauses keep full force over engine-generated outputs at the two sites), three guardrails-plan corpus/consumer conflations fixed, two residual example filenames swept, note date corrected. Remaining name carriers: frozen records (disclosed in rule), captures (immutable), and the workstream objective field (blocked on iq-context relay #11). Next: bump 0.4.0 and drive the release through scripts/release-approved-runtime.py with both consumer roots.
blockers: No corpus adoption or mutation is authorized; a deterministic fingerprinted adoption plan requires later owner approval (OB-002-1).
open_questions: Should installed workflow artifacts carry a receipt or build stamp of their own? Today the installed agent doc and skill have no content stamp, so there is no local way to tell whether a copy still matches the receipt that placed it, and a hand-edit would be undetectable from the consumer side. This surfaced from an inbound ~/.claude relay that could not distinguish an installer write from a hand-edit.

Should docs/claude-skills/meeting-ingest/SKILL.md quote a single published rule source rather than restate the semantic guidance rules verbatim? Five surfaces now duplicate the rule text, and a parity test guards it in this repo, but the duplication remains a standing drift risk raised by the ~/.claude relay.
